A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lean Finder research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, a five-participant study using 128 queries, prover integration results, and ablation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline evaluations in Appendix J, Tables 10-12.

M1.justification: The query-synthesis procedure, DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL 7B embedding model, contrastive training, DPO alignment, and prover integration procedures remain unchanged. The additional experiments evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: Training sources, query modalities, real-user evaluation, and prover benchmarks are retained. The Lean Explore comparison filters existing test data by database membership; it does not introduce a new task or domain.

E2.justification: Appendix J substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set with Lean Search's augmentation mode, Qwen3-Embedding-8B, and Lean Explore. Tables 10-12 report actual comparisons across supported modalities; Lean Explore was previously cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The new comparisons introduce augmentation before Lean Search retrieval and a separately filtered test set requiring targets to exist in Lean Explore's database. Existing evaluation metrics, training settings, user-study design, and original test protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The DPO and synthetic-query ablations, module-wise analysis, GPT-4o preference analysis, and noisy/raw-input evaluations are retained. v1 Appendix J becomes v2 Appendix K; the added baseline comparisons do not introduce a separate ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. v2 adds point estimates using the existing reporting practice, without new seed or run-count information.

E6.justification: Tables 10-12 substantially expand the comparative results while preserving earlier scores. Table 10 reports informalized-statement R@1 of 64.2 for Lean Finder, 57.7 for Qwen3-Embedding-8B, and 31.9 for augmented Lean Search. Table 12 reports 65.7 versus 35.0 for Lean Finder and Lean Explore on a separately filtered set, not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The contrastive and DPO objectives, proof-trajectory definition, and metric formulas are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about intent-aware retrieval, the 1.4M-pair dataset, user preference, retrieval gains, and prover compatibility. The new comparisons provide additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of synthetic-query benefits, the DPO alignment-retrieval trade-off, GPT-4o's limitations, and limited prover gains remain unchanged. Appendix J reiterates the existing interpretation of strong performance across input types without introducing a new mechanism or substantive limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix J documents the augment-then-retrieve procedure and database filtering for the new comparisons. v2 also discloses NERSC resource use in its acknowledgment; existing training hyperparameters, prompts, and release plans are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Qwen3 Embedding and PDEController and explicitly compares Lean Finder with a larger general-purpose embedding model. The broader positioning around user intent and the relationship to prior Lean retrieval work remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Additional Experiments appendix and acknowledgment, updates the publication header and Kaiyu Yang's affiliation, and brings the intent-cluster table into the main method discussion. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds three comparison tables and moves v1's intent-cluster Table 7 into the main text as Table 1. Existing figures and tables are retained with repositioning and renumbering; their visual designs remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix J strengthens empirical support by addressing missing comparisons with augmented Lean Search, Lean Explore, and a larger embedding model, while explicitly distinguishing database-filtered test sets. Moving the intent-cluster table into the method section also improves accessibility. These are useful, bounded gains; the central method, user study, and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
